verdicts.strongest_argument: Every input is published, and published loudly. The NSSF-adjusted NICS series is released monthly by NSSF and headlined within days by the entire firearms trade press: the July figure of 1,061,883 / +8.5% y/y was carried by Outdoor Wire, OutdoorHub, NRA Women, GunsAmerica, Ammoland and TheFirearmBlog in the first half of August. The github CSV cited here is a third-party mirror, not a private dataset. The Feb-Apr comparator is in SWBI's own 2026-06-17 release ('handgun unit sales into the sporting goods channel increasing 23.2%... while NICS increased only 1.1%'), and the +16% consensus off an $85.1M base is in a StockStory preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 (consensus revenue $98.7M). What is genuinely unpublished is only the three-month sum aligned to SWBI's fiscal quarter and the framing as a '6.5-point acceleration' - trivial arithmetic on a headline series that four covering analysts model explicitly. And the claim's own internal evidence undercuts it: SWBI printed +26.7% revenue against NICS +1.1%, so the series has almost no explanatory power for SWBI shipments, which makes +7.7% a weak lever on a print already guided to +15-20%. Decisive tape point: each of the three monthly releases landed before today and SWBI fell through all of them - $14.76 on 2026-08-03 to $12.47 on 2026-09-03 - while RGR was flat over the same window. Either the market saw the data and discounted it, or it is pricing something SWBI-specific.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both halves are in the wire, and one of them is in SWBI-specific pre-print wire copy. Ruger's Q2 release of 2026-07-29 (net sales $158.1M, +19%) was on BusinessWire, Yahoo and Las Vegas Sun the same day, the call transcript was on Motley Fool by 2026-08-07, and - decisively - a StockStory SWBI earnings preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 already draws the read-across explicitly: 'Ruger delivered 19.3% year-on-year revenue growth, beating analyst expectations by 23%... could provide a positive read-across for the firearm industry.' The SPWH half is the same day's press release and call as the 10-Q (globenewswire 2026-09-01, transcript on Investing.com, stocktitan, Manila Times), with 'firearms up 8% and ammunition up nearly 11%' quoted in the coverage; the 10-Q's +8.7%/+9.9% category detail is a second reading of the same quarter, not a second fact. The only real residual is the specific channel-inventory framing (-45,800 distributor / -100,100 finished-goods units) and its 'shipments run ahead of retail' implication, which is standard sector analysis rather than a discovery. Note the SWBI tape gave the SPWH print nothing: +0.08% on 2026-09-02, the day after.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is mainstream news, not an obscure docket entry. Judge Hendrix's 2026-08-05 judgment in the consolidated Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF / Jensen v. ATF was covered the same day by NRA-ILA, then by Wiley's client alert, NSSF's own compliance guidance, SilencerCo, Silencer Central, Silencer Shop, the American Suppressor Association and Concealed Carry Inc, and by NPR on 2026-08-17 - it is the largest change to suppressor law since 1934 and was reported as such. The stay expiry on 2026-08-12 and DOJ's non-appeal were themselves the subject of dedicated NRA-ILA Q&A pieces on 08-12 and 08-17. The SWBI investor-day figures paired with it (+95.6% suppressor revenue growth in H1 CY2026, $700M-$950M TAM) come from a Reg FD 8-K exhibit filed 2026-07-15 - a public company filing, and I verified both figures in it directly. Two further discounts: the ruling is dated 2026-08-05, five days after SWBI's fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, so it cannot touch a single dollar of the reported numbers and can only enter through tonight's commentary; and it is genuinely two-sided - taking suppressors off the NFA expands volume but also destroys the paperwork friction and dealer-network moat that let incumbents earn on the category, and invites competition into a segment where SWBI has never disclosed a revenue dollar. Against $523.8M FY26 revenue, a category SWBI declines to size is not a large lever even doubling.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: SWBI fell on the ruling days rather than rallying: -1.74% on 08-05, -1.09% on 08-06, -2.06% on 08-07, and it was flat (-0.21%) on the 08-12 stay expiry. Whatever the market made of this, it did not bid the stock, and the front-expiry skew of -0.67 shows no unusual upside call demand either.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A disclosed suppressor revenue dollar figure large enough to matter against $523.8M, or evidence SWBI pre-shipped into the ruling before 2026-07-31; either would justify a number below 50. It cannot reach the reported quarter, only the call.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The sharpest claim in the brief and the one I can least easily find published - I searched for any note observing that SWBI's 2026-06-17 guide was set with only the May NICS print visible and found none. The underlying facts are all public (the +15-20% Q1 guide is in the Q4 call transcript on Investing.com; the three monthly NICS figures are in trade press) but the information-set argument is not drawn anywhere. Three real discounts. First, the source is misdated for part of the claim: the cited Outdoor Wire URL is /releases/2026/07/, the June release published 2026-07-06, and it cannot contain the July figure - the July release lives at /releases/2026/08/. Second, the mechanism assumes SWBI guides off industry NICS, when the company's own last print showed +26.7% revenue against NICS +1.1% and management guides off its order book and shipment plan; a manufacturer three weeks into its own quarter already knows its June shipments better than any NICS reading. Third, the street is already at +16% against a 15-20% guide, i.e. barely above the low end, so the guide's conservatism is at least partly reflected and a beat to the top end is a ~2.5% revenue surprise, not a step change. And the tape has had every monthly release: the stock is 16.4% lower than when the guide was given.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Guide given at a much higher price: SWBI is -16.35% over 20 days and -26.18% from its 52-week high, so the market has de-rated since the guide rather than marked it up on the intervening data. Options give no directional lean (skew -0.67, put/call OI 0.70, 'balanced'), which is consistent with the guide-versus-data asymmetry being unrecognised in either direction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Any published note or transcript remark connecting the guide's June-17 information set to the later NICS months would take this to 80; conversely, confirmation that SWBI guides explicitly off internal orders rather than industry checks weakens the mechanism, not the pricing, and I would leave the number but cut the size.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The NFA-check surge is the trade-press headline, not a buried line: Ammoland's August piece is literally titled 'July Gun Sales Rise 8.5% as NFA Checks More Than Double', and the July NFA figure of 130,013 / +108.8% appears in the NSSF release itself and in every monthly recap. The 95.6% suppressor growth and the $700-950M TAM are in SWBI's own 8-K exhibit filed 2026-07-15, which I verified line by line. The residual - that June/July NFA data postdates the H1 window the 95.6% covers, so the current run rate is higher - is a legitimate inference and I find it nowhere, but it is an inference on two published series that a reader of both would reach in a minute. The binding problem is size, not novelty: SWBI has never disclosed a suppressor revenue dollar (the deck gives a growth rate and a category TAM and no company figure), the segment is small enough that the company chose not to size it, and FY26 revenue was $523.8M. Doubling something unsized is not obviously worth much, and half of the June/July NFA surge sits inside the reported quarter anyway, meaning it is already implicitly inside the +15-20% guide the company reaffirmed nothing against.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a public-company earnings release from two days ago with wide same-day pickup - GlobeNewswire, Manila Times, StockTitan, MarketBeat, Cerbat Gem, and an Investing.com transcript recap headlined 'tops Q2 2026 estimates, shares jump' that carries the exact firearms/ammo category numbers. The CEO quote is from a public call. Nothing here is unpublished; the claim is an inference from a published print. What holds the number down from the 80s is that the read-across was demonstrably not paid for in SWBI: the day after SPWH's release SWBI closed +0.08%, and the one SWBI-specific pre-print preview I can find (StockStory, syndicated to Yahoo 2026-09-01) names Ruger and Clarus as comparables and does not mention Sportsman's Warehouse at all. So the fact is fully public but the specific SWBI channel has not been drawn in wire copy, and the tape shows no bid. Also note SPWH's headline was flat total comps on +0.6% sales - a retailer whose overall print was mediocre, with strength confined to two categories, is a softer read-through than the framing implies, and SPWH's +9.2% move was about its own EBITDA and margin, not about firearm units.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is the most priced claim in the brief. Ruger's Q2 release went out on BusinessWire on 2026-07-29 and was picked up the same day by Yahoo Finance, Las Vegas Sun and Quiver; the call transcript was on Motley Fool and the Globe and Mail by 2026-08-07; and the read-across to SWBI specifically is in pre-print wire copy - the StockStory preview syndicated to Yahoo on 2026-09-01 states that 'Ruger delivered 19.3% year-on-year revenue growth, beating analyst expectations by 23%, and traded up 3.3%,' adding that this 'could provide a positive read-across for the firearm industry.' Peer read-across from the only other listed pure-play firearm manufacturer, five weeks before the print, is the single most standard thing a sector analyst does; the lean-channel interpretation is textbook. It is also arithmetically the weakest lever of the bullish cluster: Ruger's channel is Ruger's channel, SWBI's own last release said channel inventory of its handguns was essentially unchanged, and Ruger's beat was ASP- and new-product-driven (ASP +10% to $384), which is company-specific execution rather than an industry shipment condition.

verdicts.strongest_argument: I checked this one and the factual core survives: I can find no SWBI-specific news in August 2026 other than the routine 2026-08-20 earnings-date alert and the FY26 annual report to shareholders, no analyst action I can date to August, and the daily tape shows no discrete gap - $14.76 on 08-03 grinding to $12.47 on 09-03 with the largest single day only -3.19%. That is real and it is unpublished as an observation. But as a *finding* it has two problems that put it near the middle rather than the bottom. First, an absence of filings is not information the market lacks - EDGAR is public, and the market is the entity that sold the stock down; nobody is mispricing SWBI because they failed to check for an 8-K. Second, and more damaging, the absence of a filed cause is not the absence of a cause, and the cross-section says something SWBI-specific is happening: over 08-19 to 09-03 RGR went $38.20 to $38.32, flat, while SWBI fell 11.7%. A steady 1-3% daily bleed on ordinary volume with an idiosyncratic 12-point underperformance of the closest peer is the signature of estimate cuts, a persistent seller, or informed positioning - and it cuts against the rest of this brief rather than with it, because it means the market has had every bullish datapoint in the other seven claims and de-rated anyway. There is also no directional mechanism attached: 'unexplained decline' does not become 'will rally on the print'. The one thing that mildly supports the claim is the option market's indifference - 25d skew -0.67 with calls marginally bid and put/call OI 0.70 - which says the sellers were not buying protection against a bad print.

interactions: Five clusters, and the brief is much less independent than eight claims suggests. (1) NSSF monthly adjusted-NICS series: SWBI-a#0 and SWBI-b#0 are the same three numbers (May 1,105,758 / Jun 1,123,006 / Jul 1,061,883) and the same +7.70% sum, differing only in framing - a#0 frames it as acceleration versus the Feb-Apr quarter, b#0 as an information-set gap against the 2026-06-17 guide. b#0 is the larger residual of the two. The NFA-category figures inside SWBI-a#2 (July 130,013, +108.8%) and SWBI-b#1 (June 166,677, July 130,013) come from the same monthly NSSF releases, so all four claims ultimately rest on one published series. (2) SWBI's 2026-07-15 Reg FD investor-day exhibit: SWBI-a#2 and SWBI-b#1 cite the identical two facts from it, +95.6% H1 CY2026 suppressor revenue growth and the $700M-$950M TAM - one document, counted twice; b#1 is the larger residual. (3) Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF: SWBI-a#2 is the legal event and SWBI-b#1 is the demand consequence of the same statutory change; they are one thesis in two halves, and neither can touch the reported May-July quarter since the judgment is dated 2026-08-05. (4) Sportsman's Warehouse Q2: SWBI-a#1's 10-Q and SWBI-b#2's press release plus call are two documents from the same filer on the same day about the same quarter - a#1's +8.7%/+9.9% and b#2's 'firearms up 8%, ammo nearly 11%' are the same two categories. (5) Ruger Q2: SWBI-a#1's inventory numbers and SWBI-b#3 are the same 2026-07-29 8-K, and b#3 is the most-published item in the brief because a SWBI-specific preview already carried the read-across. Direct contradiction worth flagging: SWBI-b#4 argues the 16.4% de-rating has no company-specific cause, while a#0, a#1, b#0, b#2 and b#3 argue a stream of positive published data landed during exactly that window. Taken together they say the market saw the bullish data and sold anyway - and the fact that RGR was flat over 08-19 to 09-03 while SWBI fell 11.7% makes the de-rating idiosyncratic, which is evidence for a SWBI-specific negative that none of the seven bullish claims addresses. Finally, one source-date defect: SWBI-b#0 cites theoutdoorwire.com/releases/2026/07/ (the June release, published 2026-07-06) as the source for a July datapoint that was not published until the 2026-08 release at /releases/2026/08/; and SWBI-a#0's github CSV is a third-party mirror of the same NSSF releases rather than a primary or private source, which is why neither claim can be treated as resting on non-public data.
